channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Almaty Hosts Discussion on Role and Future of Maslikhats Amid Constitutional Reform
item.description: An expert meeting in Almaty discussed the role and future of local representative bodies (maslikhats) in light of constitutional reform. Participants examined the current electoral system, the independence of campaigns, and the maslikhats' function in representing regional interests and addressing public concerns.

item.title: Cannavaro Discusses Future with Uzbekistan National Team Management
item.description: Fabio Cannavaro stated he needs to discuss his future with the management of the Uzbekistan Football Association (UFA). In an interview with Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport, he also commented on player Abdukodir Khusanov and the national team's performance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Law on Mobilization Preparation and Mobilization
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan has approved a law on "Mobilization Preparation and Mobilization." The legislation outlines how the state should prepare for potential military threats and ensure the country's functioning during mobilization. It covers not only military conscription but also the mobilization of economic, transport, and healthcare resources.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Traffic Restrictions Based on License Plate Numbers to Improve Air Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ecology Committee has proposed temporary restrictions on vehicle movement, including odd-even license plate days, during periods of poor air quality. The measures aim to implement the 'Clean Air' national project, with exceptions for electric vehicles and special transport.

item.title: Police arrest suspect in fatal house fire in Almaty
item.description: Police have arrested a 37-year-old woman suspected of intentionally setting fire to a private house in Almaty's Bostandyk district. The blaze resulted in the deaths of five people. The suspect has been placed in a temporary detention facility.

item.title: Herat section of TAPI gas pipeline project nears completion
item.description: Construction on the Herat section of the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline project is nearing completion, with 92% of the work finished. Approximately 142.9 kilometers of the 150-kilometer pipeline have been laid and welded. Installation of equipment and construction of related facilities are also progressing significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan may grant tax and credit benefits to citizens called up for military service during mobilization
item.description: A draft law in Uzbekistan proposes tax and other mandatory payment exemptions for citizens called up for military service during mobilization. It also suggests deferring credit payment deadlines and preserving employment for mobilized citizens. The bill aims to provide financial relief and support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Sanctions Control, Tax Service Gains New Powers
item.description: Starting December 5, 2026, Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service can suspend businesses' access to electronic invoices and deregister cash registers if sanctions risks are identified. The government approved six grounds for suspension, including fictitious supplies and lack of export confirmation, to bolster economic and financial stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Secures Two Golds at Astana Para Taekwondo Grand Prix Finals
item.description: Uzbekistan claimed two gold and three silver medals at the Astana Para Taekwondo Grand Prix Finals. Guljonoy Naimova and Asadbek Toshtemirov won gold in their respective categories. Kazakhstan's para taekwondo athletes were eliminated in the quarterfinals. The event is a qualifier for the 2028 Paralympic Games.

item.title: Explosion Near Afghan School Kills Seven Students, Wounds Nearly 100
item.description: An explosion near a secondary school in Afghanistan's Kunar province has resulted in the deaths of seven students and injured up to 99 others, according to Reuters citing Taliban interior ministry spokesman Abdul Matin Qani. Local media reported significantly higher casualties, with some sources indicating at least 25 dead and 50 wounded. The exact location and circumstances of the blast remain unclear, with investigations underway.

item.title: Land Dispute in Uruzgan Province Results in Two Deaths, Two Wounded
item.description: Two people were killed and two others injured in a land dispute between two families in the Dehrawud District of Uruzgan Province, according to Bilal Uruzgani, spokesperson for the Taliban's provincial police command. The incident occurred on Friday, November 27, when members of one family opened fire on the other during the dispute. This follows similar clashes in the province that have also resulted in casualties.

item.title: Tajikistan U-17 Team Faces Italy in World Cup Round of 16
item.description: Tajikistan's U-17 national football team will play Italy in the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup in Qatar. This marks the team's first knockout stage appearance in 19 years. Tajikistan advanced after securing a draw against Senegal in their final group match.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Invest Trillions of Tenge in Transit Corridor Upgrades
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate over 2 trillion tenge for the development of transit road corridors within the next three years. The Ministry of Transport detailed plans to improve routes like "Aktobe – Kyzylorda" and "Beyneu – Saksaulsky." Additionally, 37 border crossing points within the EAEU will be modernized by 2027 to double throughput capacity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Bill to Extend Land Lease Period to 49 Years
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis has approved a bill to systematize land rights, extending the maximum land lease period to 49 years. The amendments aim to simplify land use as a market asset, prevent illegal seizures, and clarify conditions for using and consolidating land plots. The law also enhances penalties for landowners and tenants who fail to prevent land encroachment.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Almaty Arson Case That Killed Five, Including Two Uzbek Citizens
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has been detained in Almaty as a suspect in a house fire that killed five people, including two Uzbek citizens. Police identified her through surveillance footage. Investigators believe the fire was intentionally set due to personal animosity. The suspect is in custody pending further investigation.

item.title: Woman Arrested in Connection with Deadly Almaty Fire That Killed Five
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has been arrested in Almaty in connection with a fatal fire that claimed the lives of five people, including a minor. Police suspect the fire was intentionally set due to a personal dispute. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Foreign Students at Unaccredited Kyrgyz Medical Schools Given One Month to Transfer
item.description: Foreign students at unaccredited medical universities in Kyrgyzstan will have 30 days to transfer to other institutions. They can re-register their visas without leaving the country. The government has tasked ministries with facilitating the transfer process.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry Fails to Launch E-Residency for Foreigners
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has not yet launched the e-Residency platform, which would allow foreigners to obtain personal identification numbers remotely. This delay, despite a government directive over a year ago, creates bureaucratic hurdles for the growing number of foreign visitors.

item.title: Osh, Kyrgyzstan Approves Conversion of 15 Hectares of Farmland for Housing
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has approved the conversion of 15.47 hectares of irrigated farmland in Osh for the construction of multi-story residential buildings and educational facilities. The land, privately owned, will be reclassified from agricultural to settlement land, with conditions for agricultural land replacement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Tax Official Arrested for Demanding $1 Million Bribe
item.description: A tax official from the Tashkent region was detained in Tashkent while attempting to receive an advance payment of $40,000. The 38-year-old official allegedly promised to re-register a workshop and 3.5 hectares of land in Nurafshan city and obtain permits for construction work. He reportedly demanded $1.05 million for these services. Criminal charges have been filed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Deportation for Foreigners Working Without Permits
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved amendments that could lead to the deportation of foreigners working without proper permits or violating their terms. Repeat offenders or those failing to pay fines may face expulsion and a three-year entry ban. The new regulations aim to improve oversight of foreign labor.

item.title: UN Human Rights Committee Orders Kyrgyzstan to Compensate Politician Omurbek Tekebaev
item.description: The UN Human Rights Committee has ruled that Kyrgyzstan must compensate politician Omurbek Tekebaev for his 2017 prosecution. The committee found violations of his rights to adequate time for defense preparation and legal aid. Kyrgyzstan is ordered to provide compensation and take measures to prevent future violations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to upgrade consulate in Afghanistan to General Consulate
item.description: Uzbekistan's consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan, will be elevated to a General Consulate starting December 1, 2026. This move aims to foster trade and economic ties and enhance consular services, according to the Uzbek Foreign Ministry.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to increase pensions for customs officers starting December 2026
item.description: Starting December 1, 2026, Kyrgyzstan will raise pensions for former customs officers. The average increase will be around 10,000 soms, potentially doubling the minimum pension to approximately 20,000 soms. This applies to both minimum and maximum pension recipients.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Primary Healthcare Facilities Rated 57% Ready, UNICEF Study Finds
item.description: A national study by Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health and UNICEF assessed 362 primary healthcare facilities across the country. While 92% have basic medical equipment, overall readiness to provide services is only 57%. Significant gaps exist in diagnostics and essential medicines. Some facilities lacked water supply, and over a third had no transport for emergencies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Mobilization Law, Defining Legal Framework
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis approved the law "On Mobilization Preparedness and Mobilization" on November 27. The law establishes legal grounds for preparing the state, economy, and population for potential military threats. It clarifies the powers and responsibilities of state bodies, organizations, and citizens in defense readiness during peacetime and emergencies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Cabinet Halves Land Zoning Area for Ala-Too Resort Project
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet has approved changes to the functional zoning of the Issyk-Kul biosphere territory for the 'Ala-Too Resort' project. The land area to be reclassified from buffer to transitional zone has been reduced by 51.3%, from 10,462.28 to 5,097.4 hectares, excluding the largest plot in Karkyra.

item.title: Hackers Breach US Air Force Data Platform Cloud One
item.description: Hackers have breached the US Air Force's critical data platform, Cloud One. The intrusion was detected during recent platform updates, leading to the suspension of administrative and auxiliary program transfers. The incident caused disruptions to the entire system's operation.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Declare 2027 a 'Special Year' for Business Support
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank head announced that 2027 will be a special year dedicated to enhancing business support. The goal is to double per capita income to $10,000 within ten years by focusing on qualitative support for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly in finance, IT, and logistics. Plans include export assistance and incentives for banks financing SMEs.

item.title: Qatar Proposes Gulf-Iran Summit to Form Regional Defense Alliance
item.description: Former Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani has proposed a summit of Gulf leaders with Iran to establish a unified regional defense bloc. He urged GCC countries to engage in direct dialogue with Tehran on shared interests and regional security, warning that continued conflict poses significant economic and defense risks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Harsher Penalties for Drunk Driving and Reckless Driving
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved stricter penalties for traffic violations, including jail time for repeat drunk driving offenses and criminal liability for allowing minors to drive. Fines for significant speeding will also increase. These measures aim to enhance road safety following a rise in related incidents.

item.title: Seven Students Killed in Blast Near School in Afghanistan's Kunar Province
item.description: Seven students were killed and up to 99 others injured in an explosion near a school in Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province on November 28. Initial information suggests the blast occurred at a warehouse storing explosives belonging to mining companies near the school. Authorities are investigating the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves Law Penalizing Entry into Unfinished Apartment Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved a law introducing stricter penalties for unauthorized entry into unfinished apartment buildings. The new legislation aims to prevent citizens from occupying buildings that have not met construction, utility, or registration requirements. Officials and contractors found responsible for allowing such occupation could face up to three years in prison.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet to Temporarily Seize Budgetary Funds for One Year
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a mechanism to temporarily seize funds from special accounts of budgetary institutions for at least one year to finance additional republican budget expenditures. The state is obligated to return these funds no earlier than one year after seizure.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Former State Security Officials Receive Sentences Up to 17 Years
item.description: A military court in Uzbekistan has sentenced former State Security Service (SGB) officials to prison terms ranging from 15 to 17 years. Former deputy chairman Gayratulla Yeziev received 15 years, while another official, Alijon Ashurov, was sentenced to 17 years for extortion and abuse of power. Charges included bribery, illegal detention, document forgery, and torture.

item.title: Tajikistan's Civil Aviation Head Emphasizes Importance of Accident Investigation Quality
item.description: Habibullo Nazarzoda, head of Tajikistan's Civil Aviation Agency, stressed the growing importance of high-quality investigations for flight safety at a Moscow conference. He noted that ICAO standards aim to prevent recurrence of incidents. The conference also marked the 35th anniversary of the Interstate Aviation Committee (IAC), which has investigated over 1000 aviation incidents globally.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Activist Sanjar Bokayev Sentenced to 10 Years for Fraud and Other Charges
item.description: Public figure Sanjar Bokayev has been sentenced to 10 years in a medium-security prison in Kazakhstan after being found guilty of fraud, theft, spreading false information, and illegal logging. He was acquitted of money laundering due to the statute of limitations. The court also banned him from public activities for 10 years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Nearly 5kg of Drugs and Weapons Found in Vehicle in Jumgal District
item.description: Authorities in Kyrgyzstan's Naryn region seized nearly five kilograms of a suspected narcotic substance and a firearm from a vehicle. The vehicle was stopped on November 18th. Three men were found to have consumed drugs. Investigations are ongoing, with chemical and ballistic examinations ordered for the seized items.

item.title: Uzbekistan reduces roads needing repair to below 20 percent, says Road Committee head
item.description: The head of Uzbekistan's Road Committee, Jamshid Tursunov, stated that the proportion of roads requiring repair has decreased from 70% ten years ago to below 20% currently. He affirmed that President Mirziyoyev's directives on road development, emphasizing quality and safety, will be fully implemented.

item.title: Explosion Near Kunar School Kills 10, Injures 110
item.description: An explosion near a school in Afghanistan's Kunar province killed 10 people and injured 110. The Ministry of Interior stated the blast occurred in Asadabad when explosives stored for mining operations detonated due to negligence. Investigations are ongoing.
